title: Ronnie Settles It: The Neighborly Hour
description: Ronnie reads listeners' neighbor and HOA nightmares aloud and solves every one with a committee, a meeting, and the official minutes. Barry keeps explaining how lawsuits start. Ronnie keeps not hearing him.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Good evening, neighbors, and welcome to The Neighborly Hour, where YOU mail in the dispute, and I, a man who basically ran an H O A, settle it. Calmly. By the book.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, just so the people at home know, you have never actually read a bylaw.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: I have FELT every bylaw, Barry. That's deeper. <p:0.3> Our first letter, please.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Dolores from Maple Court writes, quote, my neighbor's hedge has crept eighteen inches over the line and it scratches my car every single time I pull in. I've asked nicely three times. Nothing. End quote.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Okay, that one's easy, the hedge is on her property, she can trim it.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Whoa. WHOA. Trim it herself? Dolores, do not touch one leaf. That is unilateral, and we are a community.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: What you want is to form a Hedge Subcommittee. Schedule a quarterly boundary survey. And, above all, you put the encroachment in the minutes. Now it's official.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, the hedge is still growing while you say this. The minutes don't... they don't prune anything.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Paper is patient, Barry. <p:0.3> Next letter.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Gerald in Unit twelve B writes, quote, the new neighbor parks across two spots every night, including half of mine, and after my shift I circle the lot for twenty minutes just to get home. End quote.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Poor guy. He just wants his own assigned spot.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: See, I read this as a spacing efficiency issue. Gerald, park CLOSER. Assert the spot. Get right up in there.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Leave a note, firm but warm, and laminate it. <p:0.3> I use a Gleamtech home laminator, eleven bucks, seals a grievance like a tomb. Then we motion to repaint the lines two inches over, so technically everyone is wrong.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That guarantees a scraped door, Ronnie. You've described how to get keyed.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And if he keys it? We put THAT in the minutes too. Airtight.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Aunt Pam from the cul-de-sac writes, quote, my neighbor runs a leaf blower at six in the morning every day, including Sundays. I haven't slept past dawn in a month and I am genuinely fraying. End quote.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: She sounds exhausted. Six in the morning, that's brutal.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You know who idled a truck by my mailbox once? Dennis. Just sat there. Engine going. <p:0.3> Dennis knew what he was doing, Barry.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Pam did not ask about Dennis, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: So here's the move, Pam. You fight noise with process. Draft a Sound Ordinance Proposal. Table it. Bring it to a vote in the spring.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: The spring. So the blower just... runs until the spring.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And then it's on RECORD, Barry. <p:0.3> Next.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Marcus on Birchwood writes, quote, my wife and I are fighting nonstop. She wants the front door teal, the H O A only approved the Approved Neutrals, and honestly the stress is hurting our marriage. End quote.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Okay, this one's not even really about the door. They need to talk to each other.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Marcus, I'll be honest with you. Your marriage is out of compliance.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It's WHAT?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Form a two person committee. Elect officers. And we enter the disagreement, and frankly the wife specifically, into the minutes for the record.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, you cannot minute a marriage.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You can minute anything, Barry. <p:0.3> Last letter of the night.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Howard writes, and you can tell he's panicking, quote, there is RIGHT NOW a grease fire on my neighbor's shared back deck, it is spreading, what do I do, please. He signs off, concerned but hopeful. End quote.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie. Ronnie, there's a FIRE. You tell him to call the fire department.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: First of all, Howard? Beautiful documentation. You captured the scene, you noted the time. That's leadership.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Now, do NOT call anyone before the proper channel is followed. Convene an emergency session. Appoint a fire liaison. And get that blaze into the minutes while it's still fresh.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It is still fresh because IT IS ON FIRE, Ronnie! Just say call the fire department!

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Barry, you're agitated, which is perfect, because I'm naming you our official minute taker. Grab a pen.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: So just to confirm. Our advice to a man on fire was a meeting.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Catered, ideally. Coffee, a danish. <p:0.3> We'll put it in the minutes.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: There are no minutes, Ronnie. There was never a meeting. There's just you, and a hedge that's coming for all of us.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Motion to adjourn. Seconded. Lovely. <p:0.3> Same time next week, neighbors.
